# 1.3. Exercises

## Chain Rule

In the following question, we are going to find the derivative of a long chain of functions in two ways. First we will differentiate symbolically, to compute an explicit formula, and then plug in our value of interest. Then, we will emualate automatic differentiation; this is the process by which modern machine learning libraries compute derivatives at a given point.

The function in question is K(x) = (((x<sup>2</sup> + 1)<sup>2</sup> + 2)<sup>2</sup> + 3)<sup>2</sup> + 4 and we want to know its derivative at x = -1.

<div id='mcq_chain1'></div>
<script>
generateQuiz(
    'mcq_chain1',
    'Chain rule step 1',
    `What is the derivative of f(x) = x<sup>2</sup> + 1 with respect to x?`,
    {
        '2x': '',
        'x': 'You forgot the power rule.',
        '2': 'The derivative is not constant.',
        'x<sup>2</sup>': 'This is the original function, not its derivative.'
    },
    '2x'
);
</script>

<div id='mcq_chain2'></div>
<script>
generateQuiz(
    'mcq_chain2',
    'Chain rule step 2',
    `Which of the following correctly describes K(x)?`,
    {
        'K(x) = f(g(h(k(x))))': 'This reverses the order of composition.',
        'K(x) = k(h(g(f(x))))': '',
        'K(x) = k(g(h(f(x))))': 'The middle functions are in the wrong order.',
        'K(x) = h(k(g(f(x))))': 'This composition order is incorrect.'
    },
    'K(x) = k(h(g(f(x))))'
);
</script>

<div id='mcq_chain3'></div>
<script>
generateQuiz(
    'mcq_chain3',
    'Chain rule step 3',
    `Let G(x) = g(f(x)). Which expression correctly gives G'(x)?`,
    {
        'G\'(x) = g\'(x)f\'(x)': 'Be careful: g\' must be evaluated at f(x), not x.',
        'G\'(x) = g\'(f(x)) · f\'(x)': '',
        'G\'(x) = g(f(x))': 'This is just the original function.',
        'G\'(x) = g\'(f(x)) + f\'(x)': 'Chain rule uses multiplication, not addition.'
    },
    'G\'(x) = g\'(f(x)) · f\'(x)'
);
</script>

<div id='mcq_chain4'></div>
<script>
generateQuiz(
    'mcq_chain4',
    'Chain rule step 4',
    `Let H(x) = h(G(x)). Which expression correctly gives H'(x)?`,
    {
        'H\'(x) = h\'(x)G\'(x)': 'h\' must be evaluated at G(x).',
        'H\'(x) = h\'(G(x)) · G\'(x)': '',
        'H\'(x) = h(G(x))': 'This is not the derivative.',
        'H\'(x) = h\'(G(x)) + G\'(x)': 'Chain rule requires multiplication.'
    },
    'H\'(x) = h\'(G(x)) · G\'(x)'
);
</script>

<div id='mcq_chain5'></div>
<script>
generateQuiz(
    'mcq_chain5',
    'Chain rule step 5',
    `Which expression correctly gives K'(x)?`,
    {
        'K\'(x) = k\'(x)H\'(x)': 'k\' must be evaluated at H(x).',
        'K\'(x) = k(H(x))': 'This is K(x), not K\'(x).',
        'K\'(x) = k\'(H(x)) + H\'(x)': 'Chain rule uses multiplication.',
        'K\'(x) = k\'(H(x)) · H\'(x)': ''
    },
    'K\'(x) = k\'(H(x)) · H\'(x)'
);
</script>

<div id='mcq_chain6'></div>
<script>
generateQuiz(
    'mcq_chain6',
    'Chain Rule Step 6',
    `Which of the following is the correct expression for K'(x)? Use your responses to the above questions, and write the final answer as an explicit symbolic expression in x.`,
    {
        '16x<sup>15</sup> + 112x<sup>13</sup> + 432x<sup>11</sup> + 1040x<sup>9</sup> + 1760x<sup>7</sup> + 2016x<sup>5</sup> + 1536x<sup>3</sup> + 576x':
            '',

        '16x<sup>15</sup> + 112x<sup>13</sup> + 432x<sup>11</sup> + 1040x<sup>9</sup> + 1760x<sup>7</sup> + 2016x<sup>5</sup> + 1536x<sup>3</sup>':
            'Close, but you are missing one term.',

        '15x<sup>16</sup> + 13x<sup>14</sup> + 11x<sup>12</sup> + 9x<sup>10</sup> + 7x<sup>8</sup> + 5x<sup>6</sup> + 3x<sup>4</sup> + x<sup>2</sup>':
            `The powers don't look right.`,

        '8x<sup>15</sup> + 56x<sup>13</sup> + 216x<sup>11</sup> + 520x<sup>9</sup> + 880x<sup>7</sup> + 1008x<sup>5</sup> + 768x<sup>3</sup> + 288x':
            'These coefficients are all exactly half of the correct values. Did you miss something?',

        '16x<sup>14</sup> + 112x<sup>12</sup> + 432x<sup>10</sup> + 1040x<sup>8</sup> + 1760x<sup>6</sup> + 2016x<sup>4</sup> + 1536x<sup>2</sup> + 576':
            `The powers don't look right.`
    },
    '16x<sup>15</sup> + 112x<sup>13</sup> + 432x<sup>11</sup> + 1040x<sup>9</sup> + 1760x<sup>7</sup> + 2016x<sup>5</sup> + 1536x<sup>3</sup> + 576x'
);
</script>

<div id='mcq_chain7'></div>
<script>
generateQuiz(
    'mcq_chain7',
    'Chain rule step 7',
    `What is the value of K'(-1)?`,
    {
        '-7488': 'Correct! Multiplying all chain-rule factors gives -7488.',
        '7488': `Close, but you missed the negative sign from f\'(-1) = -2.`,
        '-3744': 'Check your multiplication.',
        '0': 'None of the derivative factors are zero.'
    },
    '-7488'
);
</script>

<b>
Phew, that was a lot of work! And the explicit formula in terms of x was quite long, even when we just chained four simple functions together. Thankfully, if we only care about the value of the derivative at a point, there is a better way.
</b>
<br><br>

Let f,g,h,k and K be as before and remember f'(x) = g'(x) = h'(x) = k'(x) = 2x.

<div id='fwd'></div>
<script>
generateQuiz(
    'fwd',
    'Forward Pass',
    `
    Fill out the diagram below as the input value x = -1 gets successively transformed into the output by applying f, g, h and k in that order. The entries should all be (real) numbers and not symbolic expressions involving x. <br><br>

    <img src="../../static/module1/fwd.png" width="900">

    <br><br>

    What should be the value in the last box?
    `,
    {
        '3300': 'Try again.',
        '625': 'Try again.',
        '1525': '',
        '-150': 'Try again.'
    },
    '1525'
);
</script>

<div id='bwd'></div>
<script>
generateQuiz(
    'bwd',
    'Backward Pass',
    `
    Now we go from right to left, a 'backward' pass. Under each box is a particular derivative needed for the chain rule calculation, evaluated at the appropriate point. Fill in the boxes one-by-one using the numbers from the previous boxes, and recalling f'(x) = g'(x) = h'(x) = k'(x) = 2x. <br><br>

    <img src="../../static/module1/bwd.png" width="900">

    <br><br>

    Finally, multiply all the numbers you filled in for this second image. <br><br>
    `,
    {
        '3744': 'Try again.',
        '-7488': '',
        '7488': 'Try again.',
        '1000': 'Try again.'
    },
    '-7488'
);
</script>

Did we get the same final answer? What was the most complicated symbolic expression you had to write down for the second approach? Which method would you rather use if you had a chain of 100 functions involving sine, cosine, logarithms and exponents?
